topic: Why is the sum of the first n odd numbers always a perfect square?

scenes.title: Intro
scenes.purpose: Hook with the raw pattern and promise an explanation.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Partial sums of consecutive odd numbers appear to be exactly the perfect squares.
scenes.animation: Title writes on, then four sum rows fade in and their results are shown to be squares.
scenes.text: WHY IS EVERY RUN OF ODD NUMBERS A PERFECT SQUARE?
scenes.transition: Cut to the roadmap.

scenes.title: Roadmap
scenes.purpose: Expose the repetitive structure of the video up front.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: The argument is: observe, verify on many cases, then prove the general step.
scenes.animation: Chapter list fades in row by row; the block of worked-example chapters is boxed.
scenes.transition: Cut to the setup.

scenes.title: The Setup
scenes.purpose: Pin down the two ideas: odd numbers and the running partial sum.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Odd numbers are 1,3,5,7,...; a partial sum adds the first few of them in order.
scenes.animation: Odd numbers are marked on a line; a running total ticks 1, 4, 9 as unit squares are added.
scenes.transition: Cut to the master build.

scenes.title: Master Build
scenes.purpose: Show the entire idea once, slowly and without interruption, from 1 to 6 squared.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Six successive odd-sized L-layers stack into a 6x6 square while the running total tracks 1,4,9,16,25,36.
scenes.animation: Layers 1,3,5,7,9,11 fade on one at a time; two counters track the odd number and the running total.
scenes.transition: Cut to Example 1.

scenes.title: Example 1 — 2²
scenes.purpose: Worked case 1 of 9, identical template: 1 + 3 = 2².
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Wrapping a 1x1 square in an L of 3 cells yields a 2x2 square.
scenes.animation: The shared example template: start square, count the L, transform the outline, log the ledger row.
scenes.camera: Static landscape frame, grid on the left, ledger on the right.
scenes.transition: Cut to the next example, same layout.

scenes.title: Pattern Check
scenes.purpose: Read the pattern back off the list of squares: the gaps are the odd numbers.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Consecutive perfect squares differ by consecutive odd numbers.
scenes.animation: Squares 1²..8² stack up; curved arrows between them are labelled with the differences 3,5,7,...
scenes.transition: Cut to the big-jump stress test.

scenes.title: Big Jump — n = 12
scenes.purpose: Stress-test the pattern far from the small cases.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: The first twelve odd numbers sum to 144 = 12^2.
scenes.animation: Twelve L-layers snap on in sequence while a counter runs 1, 4, 9, ..., 144.
scenes.transition: Cut to the general reason.

scenes.title: The Reason
scenes.purpose: Show, for a generic n, that wrapping an n x n square in an L of 2n+1 gives (n+1) x (n+1).
scenes.mathematicalConcept: The next gnomon of a square grid has exactly 2n+1 cells, so n^2 + (2n+1) = (n+1)^2.
scenes.animation: A generic square is drawn, an L of 2n+1 is wrapped around it, and the outline becomes (n+1) x (n+1).
scenes.transition: Cut to the three-ways view.

scenes.title: 2n + 1, Three Ways
scenes.purpose: Confirm the L-count 2n+1 from three independent directions.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: 2n+1 as a cell count, as a difference of squares, and as the step between odd numbers.
scenes.animation: Three short arguments fade in one at a time; their conclusions are all 2n+1.
scenes.text: count it / subtract squares / walk the odds
scenes.transition: Cut to the algebra.

scenes.title: The Algebra
scenes.purpose: Chain the single step into the full identity by telescoping.
scenes.animation: Expand (n+1)^2, isolate 2n+1, then stack 1=1^2, 1+3=2^2, ... with linking + (2k+1) arrows.
scenes.transition: Cut to the recap.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.purpose: Restate every example and the single reason behind them.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Every worked case is one instance of n^2 + (2n+1) = (n+1)^2.
scenes.animation: The example ledger rebuilds, the L diagram reappears small, and the reason line lands.
scenes.transition: Cut to the outro.

scenes.title: Outro
scenes.purpose: Hold the final identity and the intuition.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: The sum of the first n odd numbers equals n^2.
scenes.animation: Squares 1, 4, 9, 16 grow in sequence under the final identity.
scenes.transition: End card.
